evidence: Workbook Quality Checks!C41:D41 and Internal Quality Checks!C41:D41 require a spread across partial-quality apps. Source-level design supports gradation: task/tests/scoring.toml:5-11 uses functional/polish/visual 0.6/0.2/0.2 and functional floor 0.05; task/tests/tools/score.py:40-48 applies gates/floor then the weighted score. The frozen scorer is byte-identical to the frozen template. Parsed scored rubrics contain 145 binary functional criteria (weight 45), 4 binary recovery criteria (weight 9), and 5 five-point Likert visual criteria (weight 6). Functional prompt:11,19 and B1/B6:55,65 explicitly preserve independent observations, use simpler valid controls and avoid sibling-failure propagation. Gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-25 gates only minimal requisition/PENDING-offer creation and independent-context readback, leaving approvals and coordinated economics scored. Visual judge.toml:17-89 has anchored degree-of-quality levels. Local arithmetic-only execution of frozen score.py with explicitly hypothetical dimension inputs produced rewards 0.0000, 0.3933, 0.4200, 0.9000 and 1.0000; see per-row-review/evidence/40/synthetic-score-results.json and its exact commands and input files. These are supplied-score fixtures, not measured rewards for actual app variants. They show that the aggregator permits intermediate values, not that the configured browser judge reliably produces them. Empirical discrimination remains unmeasured. raw-evidence-index.json at SHA256 56cf3afb78d5256d0b90ebe7a89f9f3e8174d5aca3787eb918d6954d6388c1a7 states that configured reward comparisons are absent; independently checked all 307 indexed artifact hashes, zero mismatches. local/configured-inspection.log SHA256 0033f03c91c8bd03db1d3718a8b9741eb03cb22d0f251700ef3d2d9e039cf4ed:2 explicitly records NO provider grade. Its driver inspect-configured.py:22-23 launches /usr/bin/true with the constructed arguments; its 15 tests-source hashes match this frozen candidate. No runtime-evidence.json exists. qc/README.md Runtime evidence and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md Runtime/model evidence require a real hash-bound reward-discrimination record before clearance. Neither this parser/launch probe nor synthetic arithmetic can substitute; no Oracle, model or portal score is asserted.
counterexample: Source-level broken-app challenge (not executed as an app): a real server-backed ordinary offer desk with saved coordinated previews but a dead Commit action can pass the minimal gates. It should retain ordinary and preview credit while losing hro_change_net_budget (functional judge.toml:938), change lineage/settlement and successful retry outcomes; the no-commit defect must not globally erase unrelated composition facts (judge.toml:101-137). The current prompts request this separation, but no configured run demonstrates it. Conforming-alternative challenge (not executed as an app): an initially empty operational database with generated IDs and a different readable form/detail layout is expressly allowed by instruction.md:5,11 and gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-25. It should pass the gates and earn observed behavior credit. Whether the configured judge preserves those valid observations through 145 functional criteria and available tool/budget limits remains unmeasured; functional prompt:11 maps unobserved evaluator-limited outcomes to zero. This is a missing-measurement risk, not an asserted observed false failure.
suggested_fix: With authorized provider access, run the unchanged configured verifier on controlled real weak/partial/conforming app variants, retain per-criterion and final reward logs plus exact variant/source hashes, and add a current-input hash-bound reward_is_graded_not_binary_and_discriminates runtime record. Do not alter the shared reward policy or treat synthetic dimension inputs as app-grade evidence.
